note: Banco Unión only: Banco Nacional de Bolivia's site answered 503, Banco Mercantil Santa Cruz's sits behind a captcha, Banco Ganadero's refused the request (403) and BCP Bolivia's tariff page loads its figures by script, giving none to a plain request. Banco Unión's service tariff (21 October 2026) and interest-rate tariff (27 October 2026), read in full: its five personal Visa cards sold to anyone (Internacional, Internacional Mujer, Oro, Platinum and Signature), each with its yearly maintenance cost (charged in four monthly instalments) and its fixed rate in bolivianos, lower the first year and higher after: the first year's rate is written as a twelve-month introductory rate and the later one as the card's rate (the table's columns for the second and third year are printed over each other, and each card has one later figure). A cash advance at a counter or ATM costs 3% of it. The Internacional Convenio (for employers' agreements) and BOOM Funcionario Busa (for staff) cards depend on conditions the game doesn't check, and the Empresarial is a business card, so they aren't written. No minimum payment, grace period, late fee or foreign transaction fee is stated. Wave 4 (30 October 2026) added Banco FIE and Banco Fortaleza, the two other banks among the card issuers in the ASFI's standardised tariff (its comparison of credit card charges by institution, at 31 January 2026) whose own tariffs a plain request reached. Banco FIE's tariff of lending rates and commissions (in force from 1 October 2026), read in full: its Clásica card at up to 28.00% a year and its Oro at up to 24.00%, on purchases and on cash advances, written at those figures; the account maintenance charge, nothing for the first twelve months and then 25 bolivianos a month (Clásica) or 60 (Oro), written as a monthly fee waived for its first twelve months; a cash advance costs 3.00% at every channel; operations abroad cost nothing, written as a foreign transaction fee of 0. Banco Fortaleza's external tariff (version 18, in force from 1 October 2026), read in full: its card rate, a fixed 24.00% a year (its maximum lending rates); the monthly maintenance of the Mastercard Standard, 25 to 80 bolivianos by the card's limit (up to 15,000, 30,000, 60,000 and above), written at its top, 80, and of the Mastercard Black, 125 (200 for promotional Black cards, not written; the Business Key and Business Concierge are business cards). The ASFI's register gives Fortaleza's cash advance charge, 3%, and its charge on a balance over the purchase limit, 10%, written as a share of the excess. Neither bank states a minimum payment, grace period or late fee. The ASFI register (which gives fees but no interest) also lists Banco Nacional de Bolivia, Banco Mercantil Santa Cruz, BISA, BCP Bolivia, Banco Económico and Banco Ganadero; none is written, since none of their rates was reached: BCP Bolivia's credit card tariff page loads its figures by script, BISA's and Banco Económico's home pages answered but weren't searched for a tariff in this pass, and the others as before. No minimum payment is published for Banco FIE's, Banco Fortaleza's and Banco Unión's cards; tried (wave 5, 30 October 2026): every document this file cites, downloaded again on 30 October 2026 and searched for a minimum payment, states none for them; no web search was made for them in this wave, the searches shared by every agent having gone to the larger countries; archive.org's availability API names no snapshot of the 5 documents this file cites.
